chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Fuḍayl ibn ʿUthmān, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
Indeed, in Paradise there is a station which no servant can attain except through affliction in his body.

key_terms.الْجَنَّةِ: Paradise, the final abode of reward
key_terms.مَنْزِلَةً: a rank or station of spiritual reward

ai.seo_question: How can bodily affliction raise a believer’s rank in Paradise?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that some exalted ranks in Paradise are only attained through bodily affliction and patient endurance. It frames suffering endured by the believer as a means of spiritual elevation and reward in the Hereafter.
